summary: This is a legitimate re-run: stage 1 never executed because of an import-time undefined symbol (data_ptr<long long>), and the fix is mechanical and correct. The design is copy-safe for the judge's two-state clone (TMA map encoded per launch from the passed tensor, dispatch gated only on the state boolean ssdq_ok), so run it as one okc check with no companions. Two spec-vs-code contradictions need fixing at build time: setmaxnreg 232/160 cannot fit in the register file, and the gate ratio is 0.92 in code but 0.95 in the spec.
justification: A: The mechanism is plausible. At turn_4 the Marlin pair costs 2148/2115 us (64.5% / 42.8% of the shape) against a 306 us math floor. At T=3012 there are about 94 local routes per expert, so one 128-route M tile per expert dequantizes each weight tile about once. That moves the dequant from per-use in registers (Marlin) to once per (expert, N tile, K step), and SS wgmma m64n256k16 then runs at near tensor rate. The <=1200 us target (about 4x the floor) is reachable on paper. The expected directions are consistent with the code: the path serves only 1024 < T <= 4096, so turn_1 (T=753) stays on Marlin and first_turn (T=16384) stays on Triton. The diagnosis is right. libtorch exports data_ptr<int64_t> (long on LP64), not long long, so the .so linked but failed at dlopen (patch line 530). data_ptr<int> and data_ptr<float> are exported, so replacing them is uniformity only, which is harmless. Weakest link: the kernel has never executed. This run is the first real test of the mbarrier/TMA ring, the producer dequant into a 128B-swizzled stage, and the wgmma descriptors. The most likely outcome is an OFF at the canary or self-check, which re-measures master (neutral about 1.07). That is still readable, because the log prints the error word, the first non-finite tensor and the per-case rel-L2. Second weak point: the occupancy and parallelism shape. __launch_bounds__(THREADS,1) gives 1 CTA/SM, with 32 local experts x (N/256) tiles per GEMM, about 27% M-padding (94 -> 128) and a single producer WG doing all dequant. If the counters show a large consumer wait, the bottleneck is the producer, and fixing it belongs in stage 2.
confounders: experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: defines MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS=4096 and the shape gate that the ssdq branch nests inside. If that threshold changes, the T range served changes. It does not confound turn_4 kernel time, which is the stage's milestone.

stack-tonight-five-prefill: provides _align_parallel and the align_par_ok flag (ssdq setup goes OFF if parallel align is off), plus the zero_nonlocal_w2 flag that _experts_ssdq honours. The ssdq path reuses the parallel align, so the gate's Marlin-vs-ssdq comparison shares that cost and attribution stays clean. If align_par_ok is False in the judge run, the result is a silent master re-measure; the harvest must check the OFF line.
sglang-pipeline-parity and experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: they touch different shapes or launch paths and do not confound the turn_4 expert kernel time.
interference: No companions. This is a kind: rewrite stage judged on the replaced kernels' own time in the profile (Marlin 2148/2115 us at turn_4 vs the ssdq kernel rows), not on the headline. The path is self-gated, with an in-prepare cold-L2 A/B against master's exact Marlin block. Every failure mode prints a distinct OFF line, so both a gain and a loss can be read from the log plus the profile without a second run. With 8 prefill checks left, a companion would buy nothing that the gate medians and the producer/consumer counters do not already print.
rules_flags: No rules violation found in the design. kernel_fn dispatches on the shape (tokens > SSDQ_MIN_TOKENS) and on the state boolean ssdq_ok only. It has no pointer-equality or 'live' gate, so the judge's clone of the state keeps the path on. Keep it that way: do not add a data_ptr or id() comparison, or a key-presence check on a cloned sub-dict.

The TMA map is encoded per launch on the host from the passed activation tensor and handed over as __grid_constant__. Weight, scale, error-word and counter pointers are kernel args taken from the state's own (cloned) tensors, so the design is copy-safe. The only static is the cached cuTensorMapEncodeTiled driver function pointer, which is not a device pointer and is fine.

state['ssdq_ext'] holds a Python extension module. The moe s5 judge-copy model treats the ext as shared by reference under the clone tree walk. If the judge ever deepcopies non-tensor leaves, this would raise. A safer option is a module-global ext handle with only the ssdq_ok bool and the tensors in state; the builder's choice.

Spec contradiction: the change paragraph says 'setmaxnreg 232/160', but the implementation dropped it (patch line 67) because 2x232x128 + 160x128 = 79,872 > 65,536 registers per SM. Do NOT add setmaxnreg 232/160; it would fault or fail to launch. If setmaxnreg is wanted, use a split that fits, such as consumers 232 and producer 40 (64,512 registers), which is a stage-2 matter.

Spec contradiction: the gate ratio is 0.92 in code (SSDQ_GATE_RATIO) but 0.95 in the change paragraph. Pick one and make the printed PATH CHOSEN text match the constant; the code currently hard-codes '0.92x' in the string.

kernel_fn allocates xs, c1 and c2 at block_experts.shape[0]*128 rows. _align_parallel's cap is computed from n and local_count, so these sizes depend on shape only and are fine. The torch.zeros for y when zero_nonlocal_w2 is set is shape-sized, also fine.
open_questions: After the fix, grep the built C++ string for 'data_ptr<' (the planned prepare audit). Also confirm that any at::Tensor accessor with a template (e.g. size<>, item<>) is absent, since those could hit the same long/long long trap.

If the canary passes but the self-check fails, is the bound max(2x Marlin rel-L2, 8e-3) tight enough to separate a swizzle or descriptor bug from fp32-accumulation noise? The per-case print gives both numbers; read them before minting stage 2.
Harvest: confirm the profile shows the ssdq kernel row at turn_4 and that Marlin is absent there. A PATH CHOSEN=ssdq line alone is not proof (moe s4 lesson).
SSDQ_BUDGET_S=170 s plus about 31 s of compile: does prepare() on current master (with the stack-tonight-five checks) leave room, or will the run go OFF for budget before it builds?
